minutes.headline: Parks Commission voted to open the town beach June 18 and approved two geocache placements, amid friction over policy compliance.
minutes.summary: The commission approved prior minutes, heard the new rec director's update and a debate over how ambitious summer programming should be, and heard a skate park fundraising update. It pressed on non-compliance with its porta-potty and dumpster policies, approved two geocaches with a historic-site condition, voted a June 18 beach opening, and discussed Marshall Park next steps, the McNally snack shack, water district land, and Northfield Park.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to open the town beach on June 18, passing by roll call.
The commission approved two geocache placements, at Veterans Memorial Park and the town pound, on condition they stay off the historic wall and gate.
Members pressed on compliance with the porta-potty and dumpster policies; it goes on the next agenda, and the trash policy will go to the high school athletic director.
On Marshall Park, members discussed grant sources, ARPA money and phasing, disagreed on asking for local tax dollars, and set no date for a joint presentation.
The commission set its next meeting for June 15 by Zoom, when the board reorganizes.

why_it_matters: The beach opening date and the policies for portable toilets, dumpsters and trash decide when and how town recreation sites run this summer.
Marshall Park's funding is undecided between grants, ARPA and possible local tax dollars, so a future request for town money could come to residents at a Town Meeting vote.
watch_next: Next meeting June 15 at 7 via Zoom: policy compliance on the agenda and board reorganization.
Marshall Park phasing priorities, due from members before the next meeting.
